summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of chronic graft-versus-host disease, hypogammaglobulinemia, and prior stem cell transplant was admitted for acute worsening of chronic abdominal pain and dark, coffee-ground-like stools. Imaging revealed left hemicolitis with colonic wall thickening, likely infectious given her immunocompromised state. Stool studies were negative for pathogens including C. difficile, Salmonella, and parasites. She received intravenous ciprofloxacin and metronidazole, later transitioned to oral therapy. She was also treated with IVIG due to low immunoglobulin levels and being overdue for replacement. A flexible sigmoidoscopy showed normal mucosa, supporting improvement. Her symptoms resolved, and she was discharged home on a short course of oral antibiotics with follow-up planned for IVIG, ophthalmology, and SIBO testing.
